content:
maya: Quick thread to capture notes from today's hallway convo about authz slices + peering limits for private endpoints. I want to record a prototype plan before filing an RFC.
maya: Problem statement: customers want private endpoints with source-ip preservation and tenant-scoped authz. We need an approach that supports both customer-hosted slices (in their VPC) and managed slices (in our relays) without exploding peering or NAT state.
owen: Two obvious modes: 1) customer-hosted slice -> keeps source IP, fewer peering objects for us but cross-account NAT/route complexity for them. 2) managed slice -> we control routing but we SNAT, must add original-src headers.
karen: Operational constraints: AWS per-account VPC peering limit and per-region ENI limits. If we give each tenant a dedicated peering, we'll run out quickly. We need a shared-peering + logical multiplexing model.
zach: Proposed compromise: group tenants into "peering pools" by security tier. High-security tenants get dedicated peering or customer-hosted slice. Low-security tenants map to shared peering with multitenant slices and header-based provenance.
maya: Good. Also consider connection hairpin: edge -> regional relay -> peering pool -> slice. That keeps relay->router hops deterministic.
owen: About source-ip preservation: for customer-hosted slices we can preserve 5-tuple. For managed slices we must preserve evidence: inject x-redwood-original-ip + x-redwood-original-protocol and maintain signed provenance header to prevent spoofing.
karen: Security: signed provenance header needs HMAC with rotating key per-peering-pool. Rotations are a pain but manageable via central KMS. Document expiration TTL on headers (e.g., 10s).
zach: Authz latency: introspection checks are hot. We should allow local token cache on the slice with configurable TTL and a soft-stale mode so short network blips don't block auth. Soft-stale: if cache entry expired within 30s, allow check and schedule revalidation async.
maya: Right. For correctness we still record a revalidation failure metric and surface to SRE. Also, policy push vs pull: prefer push for rollout velocity but maintain pull for reconnects.
owen: Peering scaling: limit total active peerings per region and use gateway route tables + prefix-lists to multiplex L3. One pool per AZ could help ENI caps.
karen: Cert management: we should avoid long-lived tenant certs in our control plane. Use short-lived leaf certs from a shared CA; slices hold ephemeral keys in KMS/HSM if managed. Customer-hosted slices can bring their own cert but must present proof at registration.
zach: Failover semantics: define three behaviors per slice: fail-closed (deny), fail-open-central (central legacy policy), fail-open-allow (temporary lenient). Default = fail-open-central for availability, but require stricter for SOC2-high tenants.
maya: Rollback operator flow: UI toggle to disable slice, which flips route table and sets policy to central. Must also trigger cert revocation if malicious. Single-button action in console required.
owen: Observability: slices emit aggregate auth checks (counts/p95/p99) but never token payloads. Central logs should store request id, tenant id, outcome code, and provenance header hash for audits.
karen: Billing note: managed slices incur a per-slice baseline plus per-million auth checks. Product to propose SKU. Keep options: shared-multitenant discount.
zach: Prototype plan: spin a managed peering-pool in us-west-2; create two multitenant slices and one dedicated tenant slice; instrument original-ip header and signed-provenance; run 10k reqs/sec synthetic with intermittent slice outages to validate failover.
maya: Spike acceptance criteria: 1) p50/p95 auth latency overhead <1ms vs baseline 2) failover to central within 300ms on slice loss 3) no leakage of tokens in telemetry 4) peering objects < 10 per AZ for the test tenant set.
owen: I'll prepare the spike harness this week. @karen can you draft the policy schema and the provenance HMAC rotation plan?
karen: Yep. I'll also add a short runbook for "disable slice" and cert revocation steps.
zach: devops-bot: created branch "spike/authz-peering-pools" for maya, assigned to owen.
maya: thanks. After spike we'll decide RFC scope: probably authz_slice resource with mode: managed|customer-hosted|multitenant-pool, plus peering_pool resource and provenance config.
maya: tagging this for RFC-queue once spike metrics land.
